findings.title: Cleanup removes a hard-coded "alias" IdP instead of the created IdPs
findings.body: The cleanup `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` binds the literal alias "alias", not the `idp-alias-N` identity provider just created. The method reference is evaluated immediately, so the 20 IdPs created in testCacheIDPForLogin (and idp-alias-20 at line 425) are never removed. They leak into the realm and can affect other tests or re-runs. The same copy-paste defect exists in testCacheIDPByOrg (line 303), and the new test repeats it.

findings.title: remove() now always performs an extra DB lookup by alias
findings.body: `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is executed unconditionally on every remove(). Previously the delegate lookup only happened when the alias key was invalidated. The result is needed only for the login-cache invalidation, so every removal now costs an extra query even when the alias is cached or the IdP is not login-capable.

findings.title: Login predicate mixes org-aware wrapped model with raw updated model
findings.body: In update(), `idpById` comes from getById(), which returns an organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() also returns false when the bound organization is disabled. `updated` is the raw model. The two sides of the login predicate therefore use different enabled semantics. If an IdP linked to a disabled org stays enabled, the predicate flips and login caches are invalidated unnecessarily. The result is over-invalidation rather than stale data, but the comparison should use consistent models.

findings.title: REALM_ONLY and ALL cache entries are fragmented by organizationId
findings.body: searchKey is set from organizationId for every mode. For FetchMode.REALM_ONLY the delegate ignores organizationId, so each distinct organizationId value produces a separate cached query holding identical results. This wastes cache space and forces redundant DB queries for the same realm-level result set. The search key should be fixed for modes that ignore the org id.

findings.title: getForLogin javadoc omits the new BROKER_PUBLIC requirement for org-linked IdPs
findings.body: The javadoc says an IdP is usable for login if it is enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login. The PR changes getLoginPredicate() (line 254) to also require that org-linked IdPs have BROKER_PUBLIC set to true. The documented contract for getForLogin and the LoginFilter predicate are now out of sync. Callers relying on the javadoc will be misled about which IdPs are returned.
